newsitem.title: UK: LME copper above $2,200, stocks main factor.
newsitem.headline: LME copper above $2,200, stocks main factor.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) three months delivery copper price surged up to $2,200 a tonne, a five month high, in evening inter-office trading.
The move took place in a thin market and was seen as a continuation of the volatile trading conditions seen earlier in the day when the price ranged from $2,125 up to $2,180 and back below $2,140.
The debate last week over the possibility of the existence of sizeable off-market stocks in Europe appeared to found market opinion sceptical, traders said.
It was now focusing on the probability that LME stocks will on Tuesday fall below 100,000 tonnes for the first time for six years. LME stocks data will be released at 0900 GMT.
At 1900 GMT three months delivery copper was quoted at $2,210/$2,215 a tonne compared with its afternoon close on the Exchange floor at $2,159 and Friday's close of $2,148 a tonne.

Most other base metals held steady reflecting copper's strong rise but nickel, Monday's other main mover, did manage to claw back a small part of early large losses to be quoted at $6,680/$6,710, against $7,050 Friday, and an earlier low of $6,600 a tonne.
